exchange-foam.look: Label mode looks good, and it is the best reason for this node. K 3 to 8 over smooth or warped sources gives a geological map or military camouflage: blobs of very different sizes, enclaves and islands, curved boundaries, triple junctions between any two labels. The wide view shows no lattice once the per field offset is on. Over the facet source it becomes angular non-convex plates. Over fBm the edges are jagged and speckled, busier and less handsome. Over -F1 it looks like blocky weighted Voronoi and loses the point. K=16 fragments into a noisy mess. It is clearly different from warped CellularValue, whose cells keep one size and smear. Margin is an organic crack network with no point sites, but wall width varies: where the top two fields run nearly parallel the wall spreads into a blurry sheet. Its relief gives tablelands with gullies between them, which is striking. Rank and softmax are soft blurs of the same map and add little. In 3D the XZ slice looks as good as 2D, the phase volume is an organic blob network, and the margin volume at iso .5 is a packing of irregular pebbles with thin gaps.
exchange-foam.dims: Dimension agnostic: 2D and 3D measured on several sources. 4D follows the source, not rendered.
exchange-foam.range: Label k/(K-1) mapped to [-1,1] exact. Margin 2*sat(gap*gain)-1, [-1,1] exact, mean 0.36 at gain 5 and K 5. c0ratio is 1 for Label by design, 7.88 for Margin (max slope 31 at gain 5) and 7.98 for Rank.
exchange-foam.artifacts: Found and fixed: Perlin and Simplex are 0 at every lattice vertex, so seed offsets alone make all K fields tie there. At K=8, 99.9% of those vertices have 4+ labels within radius .03, against 0.2-1.1% at random points; fBm 96.8%. Visible as star junctions in Margin. A fixed per field offset takes this to 0.5% or less. Warped and facet sources do not need it (4.1%, 0.0%). Shares at K=5: 0.190..0.207 over 6 seeds and 4 sources. All label pairs touch; Terrace has 4 of 10 pairs and shares 0.020..0.490. CellularValue quantised to 5 labels also measured 0.197..0.201 and 10 of 10 pairs, so equal shares are not unique; the shape is. Margin width is not constant. K>=16: 40-67% of regions under .25 u^2. Gumbel weights hit .522-.529 for a .533 target but need the source std: -30% gives .438, +50% gives .645. A constant bias is monotonic but compressed (.46).
exchange-foam.node_shape: ExchangeFoam: Source, Phases K (2..16, default 5), Output {Label, Margin, Winner Value}, Margin Gain (hybrid), Seed Stride, internal field offset, optional Weight Ratio and Source Std, Output Min/Max. Drop Rank and Softmax. FoamBlend v2 is a strong Blend output or sibling node.
exchange-foam.port_notes: K source evals with position offset per field plus a large seed stride, masked update of m1, m2 and label, Output by Select after the loop. Gumbel needs Exp and two Logs per field, +26% scalar at K=4.

critic.notes: Label mode does look good and holds across seeds and a 64 unit wide view: blobs of very different sizes, enclaves, any-to-any junctions, no visible lattice with koff=1. With koff=0 the 4-label pinwheel points at Perlin lattice vertices are visible in the field itself, so the per-field offset is mandatory, as the prototyper found. The shape cannot be had from existing nodes: Max of seeded copies gives the winner value but there is no compare/select node to produce the label, and warped CellularValue gives convex, similar-sized cells (the family comparison image shows the difference plainly). Cost is K x source, so the default source should be something cheap (facet or Value); 5x Perlin is the honest price. Margin walls blur into sheets where the top two fields run parallel. Gumbel weights depend on a supplied source std, so ship them as an advanced option or not at all.

tournament.notes: Re-tested: check exact [-1,1], c0ratio 1 by design, far coords and 3D ok; speed Perlin K5 306.6 ns, warped 852.8, facet 85.6 (claims 317 / 874 / 88 confirmed). Label holds at seeds 7 and 11 over a 64-unit view: varied blob sizes, enclaves, any-to-any junctions, no lattice with koff=1; koff=0 shows 4-label pinwheels at Perlin vertices in the field itself, so the per-field offset is mandatory. Not buildable from existing nodes (no compare/select to emit an argmax label) and visibly different from warped CellularValue. Cost is K x source, so default to a cheap source. Margin walls blur where the top two fields run parallel. Gumbel weights need the source std: advanced option at most. Drop Rank and Softmax.

master.one_liner: Evaluate K seeds of any source and take argmax: each label gets exactly 1/K of the area with no calibration, and the interfaces form an organic lattice-free cell foam.
master.look: Label: camouflage-like blobby mosaics with triple junctions where any label can touch any other, unlike a thresholded single noise where only value-adjacent bands touch. Margin: organic crackle foam, with non-convex cells and no lattice or point sites. Rank: stacked plateaus with soft steps. Good for biome maps, camouflage, cracked mud and multi-material masks. Measured area per label for K=5: 0.199 to 0.201 on oct 1 and oct 5 sources and two seeds.
master.algorithm: s_k = Source(seed + k*prime, p), k = 0..K-1. Identically distributed fields are exchangeable, so P(argmax = k) = 1/K for any source and any histogram, and rank(s_0) is exactly uniform on 0..K-1. Track m1 and m2 (largest and second largest) and the label with Select. Outputs: Label = k/(K-1) mapped to [-1,1] or a hash of k; Margin = clamp((m1 - m2)*Gain); Rank = sum_{k>=1} smoothstep(-eps, eps, s_0 - s_k). Weighted shares (theory, not run): for sources with exactly uniform marginals, transform each to Gumbel with -log(-log(u)) and add log(w_k); the Gumbel-max property then gives exact shares w_k / sum w.
master.why_new: Biome coverage normally comes from tuning thresholds per source. This gives exact equal shares regardless of source, including warped and fractal graphs, with no measurement. Max can get the top value but no node exposes the winner index or margin. It gives a cellular look without feature points.
master.simd_plan: Fixed K, K source evals. Masked update of m1, m2 and label, no per-lane branching. Cost K x source; K=5 Perlin measured 7.5x perlin2 scalar. Dimension and tiling come from the source. Uses seed offsets, so the source graph must respond to seed.
master.continuity: Label is discontinuous by design, like CellularValue. Margin is C0 with a kink at interfaces. Rank is C1 with eps > 0.
master.params: Phases K (int), Output (Label, Margin, Rank), Margin Gain (hybrid), Softness (float), Seed Stride (int), Source. Up to 4 float weights if the Gumbel mode is added.
master.risks: Exactness is about the field's stationary law, so a source with a spatial trend or a fixed-seed sub-node shared between phases loses it. Cost scales with K. Soft rank at large K blurs towards the mean. Gumbel shares need exactly uniform inputs (PhaseVortex) or a good CoverageRemap, and are untested. Margin has no fixed relation to distance, so cell wall widths vary.
master.cost_note: Cost K x source; K=5 Perlin measured 7.5x perlin2 scalar.

queue.name: ExchangeFoam
queue.reason: argmax over K seeded sources gives exact 1/K shares: lattice-free biome labels, trivially SIMD. Judges split on wow, so the Label mode needs a look.

simplex-facet.look: Bare lattice (pw=0): exactly flat facets with straight creases, low poly at once, but every crease lies in 3 directions, so in relief ridges run as zigzags along 60 degree lines and the FFT is a hard 6 ray star. It reads as a regular quilt. In 3D the same lattice looks much better: the isosurface cuts the tets at arbitrary planes, so vol shows clean irregular planar polygons, cut crystal caves, and the lattice is hard to spot. With PL warp .5/.5 the 2D lattice is gone by eye: polygons of varied shape, facets still exactly flat, FFT star reduced to faint rays, relief reads as folded rock, with softer and more numerous creases than the cellular mesh. Flat mode with PL warp shows bent edge polygons (one base triangle cut by warp creases), not clean triangles. FBm over it (4 octaves) gives angular rocky mountains. Smoothness looked bad: star spikes at every vertex, drop it. Tilted planes and FaceOffset give shard fields with cliffs; they are a look, but not low poly terrain. GenTileable2D's 4D torus map does not keep facets flat: the tile image shows curved creases.
simplex-facet.dims: 2D, 3D and 4D measured. Facets are flat in 2D and 3D. The 4D torus map used by GenTileable2D bends creases, a limit of that mapping.
simplex-facet.range: Lerp: convex combination of rnd11 values, so [-1,1] analytically. Measured over 8 seeds -0.993..0.994 bare, -0.995..0.997 with PL warp. Mean near 0, std 0.41. Tilted plane mode overshoots and needs a scale.
simplex-facet.artifacts: Bare 2D crease normal peak/mean 5.48. PL warp .5/.5: 1.37, with 43% more crease length. Warp folds at high amplitude and frequency: 23.92% folded area at pw .6 pf 1.3, swirly. Fixed a proto bug: facet ids h*31+k gave -0.48 correlation between the two triangles of a skew cell, causing diagonal streaks in Flat mode; a port must not derive facet values by adding to the hash.
simplex-facet.node_shape: SimplexFacet: Output {Lerp, Flat, Tilted, Tent}, optional Source (LerpSource), Warp Amplitude (hybrid, default 0.5, 0 = bare lattice), Warp Frequency (0.5), Face Offset (hybrid), Slope, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. No vertex Jitter, no Smoothness.
simplex-facet.port_notes: Reuse Simplex skew and traversal, no gradients: 3/4/5 hashes and a weighted sum, branch free with existing masks. PL warp is the same location at a lower frequency, with a fixed rotation on the warp lattice in 2D, added to the position; no triangle solve, so it works in every dimension. LerpSource evaluates Source at D+1 vertices per lane.

master.one_liner: Value noise on the simplex lattice with exact barycentric (piecewise-planar) interpolation: low-poly faceted terrain and crystals directly from a noise node, with optional per-facet offsets.
master.look: Flat triangular facets with crisp fold lines, like a decimated mesh, a cut gemstone or paper origami terrain; FaceOffset adds cliffs between facets (crystal cluster, broken ice floes, shattered glass). The hillshade is flat-shaded triangles, a look that currently needs a mesh pipeline, not a noise.
master.algorithm:
Params: FaceOffset (hybrid, 0 = continuous), Smoothness (0..1 blend toward a smooth variant), Jitter (0..0.5 vertex jitter in skewed space, keeps triangles valid).
2D: s = (x+y)*F2; i = floor(x+s), j = floor(y+s); u = x+s-i, v = y+s-j (skewed cell coords in [0,1)).
  tri = u > v; vertices: V0=(i,j), V1 = tri ? (i+1,j) : (i,j+1), V2=(i+1,j+1)
  lambda = tri ? (1-u, u-v, v) : (1-v, v-u, u)      // barycentric in skewed space; skew is linear so the patch is a plane in world space
  h_k = rnd11(hash(seed, V_k)); value = Sum lambda_k h_k
  FaceOffset: value += FaceOffset * rnd11(hash(seed, i, j, tri))
3D: skew s = (x+y+z)*F3; u,v,w fractional; sort: hi = max(u,v,w), lo = min, mid = u+v+w-hi-lo; lambda = (1-hi, hi-mid, mid-lo, lo); the 4 vertices are V0, V0 + e_argmax, V0 + e_argmax + e_argmid, V0 + (1,1,1); argmax/argmid via compare masks exactly as Simplex3D's traversal does.
4D: same with 5 vertices and the rank trick already in Simplex 4D.
Smoothness: replace lambda by normalised lambda^2(3-2lambda) (C1 inside the simplex, still C0 across edges) or just lerp with SuperSimplex via graph.
Jitter: vertex world position offset by Jitter*rndvec(hash(V)) and lambda recomputed from the jittered triangle via one 2x2 (3x3) solve: optional, costs more; the unjittered version is the core.
master.why_new: Value noise with linear interpolation on a square lattice gives bilinear saddle patches (curved) with axis-aligned creases; Terrace quantises height not slope. Exact planar facets on an isotropic triangular/tetrahedral lattice are not expressible by any graph of existing nodes.
master.simd_plan: Reuses Simplex skew and vertex traversal; no gradients, 3/4/5 hashes and a weighted sum: cheaper than Simplex (2D ~0.7x Perlin, 3D ~0.8x Simplex 3D, 4D ~Simplex 4D). Branch-free via the existing compare-mask traversal. GenTileable2D works through the 4D form.
master.continuity: C0 (creases along every simplex edge) by design; discontinuous with FaceOffset > 0; Smoothness only smooths inside facets.
master.params: FaceOffset (hybrid), Smoothness, Jitter, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
master.risks: The lattice is visible by design (regular triangles); vertex Jitter breaks regularity but needs a per-sample 2x2/3x3 barycentric solve and the window argument becomes delicate (jittered vertex must stay inside its skewed cell, Jitter <= 0.5 guarantees valid triangles). Some may consider this just 'linear simplex value noise'; the facet-offset and jitter are the added value.
master.cost_note: Reuses Simplex skew and vertex traversal; no gradients, 3/4/5 hashes and a weighted sum: cheaper than Simplex (2D ~0.7x Perlin, 3D ~0.8x Simplex 3D, 4D ~Simplex 4D).

proto_index.params_text: pw=0.5,pf=0.5 (PL warp); no params = bare lattice, best for 3D volumes

queue.name: SimplexFacet
queue.reason: Barycentric value noise on the simplex lattice, cheaper than Simplex: instant low-poly (J4 top pick). Skip vertex jitter. Triangles show unless warped.

cellular-facet-mesh.look: The best 2D low poly in the family by a clear margin. Relief reads as a hand modelled low poly mesh: large clean triangles of varied size, crisp ridges, nothing lines up. Flat mode is a clean irregular triangle mosaic that CellularValue's polygons cannot give. Tent mode is a striking field of irregular triangular pyramids. Tilted is broken shards. 3D is good but no better than the far cheaper simplex lattice at equal vertex density: vol shows clean planar faces with noticeably elongated shards from the Kuhn split along one body diagonal. The 3D tent output shows the grid openly, with slots lining up across the cube, so that output is bad in 3D. Random diagonals show long slivers, and fixed diagonals show strong diagonal streaks.
cellular-facet-mesh.dims: 2D measured and good. 3D measured, works with 48 tets at J<=1/3, costly for what it gives. 4D not built, and not affordable beyond the unjittered simplex lattice, which is SimplexFacet. Tiling bends creases regardless.
cellular-facet-mesh.range: Lerp is a convex combination of rnd11 values, so [-1,1] analytically. Measured -0.989..0.995 over 8 seeds, mean 0.003. Tilted overshoots (-1.28..1.43 seen) and needs a scale.
cellular-facet-mesh.artifacts: None in Lerp at J.9. No sample outside every triangle at J .9, .98 and 1.0 with Delaunay and shorter diagonals, 1024x1024 over a 256 cell window. Crease normal peak/mean 1.09, min angle p05 17.4 deg, 2.99% triangles under 15 deg, max slope 4.78. Shorter diagonal: 1.09, 4.05%, but max slope 12.48. Random diagonal: 10.18% slivers. Fixed diagonal: peak/mean 2.14. J.6 Delaunay: no slivers, peak/mean 1.46. Same id correlation bug as simplex-facet, fixed.
cellular-facet-mesh.node_shape: CellularFacetMesh: Output {Lerp, Flat, Tilted, Tent}, optional Source (LerpSource), Jitter (0.9), Diagonal {Delaunay, Shorter, Random}, Slope, Face Offset, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. 2D-first. 3D optional, and 4D unsupported or forwarded to the simplex lattice.
cellular-facet-mesh.port_notes: Window loop over 9 corners. 4 quads: validity crosses plus in-circle, Select the corners. 8 triangles: 3 crosses, Reciprocal, max(min(lambda)) with Select, so float rounding cannot open cracks. Planarity holds for J<=1 because a row edge stays in its two cells and a column edge in its two cells, and any cell they share holds their common endpoint. 3D: 8 hexes x 6 Kuhn tets; worst signed det 0.10 at J .30 and -0.05 at J .35, so the limit is 1/3.

critic.notes: Best 2D low poly in the family at every seed I looked at: large irregular triangles, crisp ridges. Not flawless: at seed 7 a few long sliver triangles appear bottom left of the hillshade, and the 2D axis metric was 47.7 (prototyper sheet 10.9), so 'nothing lines up' is seed dependent. In 3D the Kuhn split is openly visible as an axis-aligned grid in the flat-mode XZ slice, and the 3D volume is no better than the bare simplex lattice at 12.7x the cost (prototyper number, consistent with images). 4D does not exist. Jitter 0.6 shows grid alignment; 0.75 and 0.9 look alike. Shares the whole output stage with SimplexFacet, so package it as a Lattice {Simplex, JitteredGrid} enum on one facet node with the grid option 2D/3D only.
critic.improved: Jitter sweep at seed 7 found nothing better than 0.9; gallery unchanged.

tournament.notes: Re-tested: check c0ratio 8.0, range -0.989..0.995, far coords and 3D ok; speed 87.8 ns (claim 94, confirmed). Best 2D low poly at every seed seen, but seed 7 has a few long slivers and axis metric 47.7 vs the prototyper's 10.9. 3D flat-mode XZ slice shows the Kuhn tetrahedra as an axis-aligned grid; 3D volume no better than bare simplex at ~12.7x cost (prototyper figure, consistent with images). No 4D. Same output stage as SimplexFacet, only point location differs, so ship as a Lattice {Simplex, JitteredGrid} enum, grid 2D/3D only.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: estimate: about 7-9 / 26-37 / none (2D/3D/4D). Scalar measured: 2D Delaunay 94.1 ns, shorter diagonal 83.9 ns, 3D J.33 341.8 ns (12.7x the bare simplex lattice in 3D).

artist-terrain.note: Best 2D low poly in the family: large varied triangles, crisp ridges. 3D no better than simplex-facet at ~12x the cost; no 4D.

artist-material.note: Best low poly image in the set, with big readable facets. No 4D.

voxel-engineer.note: Best 2D low poly, 12.7x cost in 3D for no gain. Lattice enum 2D only.

maintainer.note: Best 2D low poly at every seed: hand-built-mesh triangles, crisp ridges, c0 8. 3D is 12.7x the bare lattice for no gain, so 2D mode of SimplexFacet.

Measured on the node in 2D: 6.5% of the area at 0.5, 23.89% at .6 x 1.3 (the prototype measured 23.92%), 32% at 1. 3D folds 10% at 0.5 and 40% at 1. Warp lattice turned 30 degrees around Z in every dimension.

plan_node.expected_cost: Measured with fnlab bench, AVX2, 2D / 3D / 4D: default with warp 1.87 / 2.67 / 3.76 ns, bare 0.99 / 1.49 / 2.04, JitteredGrid bare 6.79 / 34.65 (4D is the simplex lattice), against Perlin 0.93 / 2.13 / 4.12 and CellularDistance 3.89 / 12.36 / 41.47 in the same run. So bare 1.1x / 0.70x / 0.50x Perlin, default 2.0x / 1.3x / 0.91x, JitteredGrid 7.3x / 16x Perlin and 1.7x / 2.8x CellularDistance. SSE41 default 3.70 / 5.53 / 7.77, AVX512 1.21 / 1.76 / 2.91.
plan_node.dims: Simplex lattice real in 2D, 3D and 4D. JitteredGrid real in 2D and 3D, and 3D costs 16x Perlin. 4D uses the simplex lattice, stated in the description, so GenTileable2D never shows the jittered mesh. GenTileable2D has no seam (fnlab tile ratio 1.07) but bends the facets.
plan_node.range: Native ranges by construction. Lerp, Flat and Tent are +-1, measured over 1M samples per dimension: Lerp -0.9952..0.9959 in 2D, -0.9858..0.9871 in 3D, Tent -1.0001..0.9994. Tilted is +-( 0.5 + Slope R ), R from the lattice geometry on Simplex and from a measured fit on JitteredGrid, with a clamp for rarer facets: measured -0.967..0.971 Simplex, -0.923..0.928 JitteredGrid in 2D.
notes: A port must not derive facet values by adding to the hash: that gave -0.48 correlation between the two triangles of a skew cell.
Critic: the PL warp at seed 7 reads as crumpled paper, busier than the prototyper said. Bare 3D is the cut-crystal image.

master.one_liner: Locate the sample in a jittered-grid triangulation (locally Delaunay diagonals) and output barycentric interpolation, flat facets, random planes or a tent per triangle: a low-poly / faceted surface evaluated pointwise.
master.look:
True low-poly terrain with straight creases (stylised game terrain), triangle mosaics, triangular crack webs, faceted hills. Lookup mode turns any FBm graph into a low-poly world. Prototyped: rel_tri modes 0-4, using an 18-triangle search rather than the fan.
[CellularFacetMesh, cell-relations] Low-poly terrain: flat triangular facets with straight creases (Lerp), shattered flat shards (Flat/Plane) or a field of irregular pyramids (Tent). Hillshaded it looks like folded paper or crystal faces, nothing on the sheet has straight creases. LerpSource turns any node into its piecewise-linear 'mesh-decimated' version.
master.algorithm:
Lattice and jitter as in CellularMeshEdges (J < 1, margin m). Quads Q(c) with corners A=P_c, B=P_{c+x}, C=P_{c+y}, D=P_{c+x+y}. Because the jittered grid graph stays planar for J<1, the quads tile the plane, and for S in cell s the containing quad has c in {s-1,s}^2 (proof: Q(c) is inside [c+m, c+2-m]^2), so only 4 quads = 8 triangles, all 9 corners in the 3x3 window.

Diagonal per quad (depends only on the 4 corners, so every sample agrees):
  adValid = cross(D-A,B-A)*cross(D-A,C-A) < 0 ;  bcValid = cross(C-B,A-B)*cross(C-B,D-B) < 0   (non-convex quad: only the diagonal through the reflex corner is valid)
  both valid: useAD = inCircle(A,B,C; D) <= 0 (3x3 determinant of relative coords, Delaunay) or a hash bit (Mode=Random)
  tris = useAD ? {ABD, ADC} : {ABC, BCD} (via Select on the corner positions, no branch)

Point location for each of the 8 triangles (p0,p1,p2) CCW:
  e0 = cross(p1-p0, S-p0); e1 = cross(p2-p1, S-p1); e2 = cross(p0-p2, S-p2)
  inside = (e0>=0)&(e1>=0)&(e2>=0); area = e0+e1+e2; lambda = (e1, e2, e0)/area
  result = Select(inside, value(T), result)   (exactly one triangle hits; on a shared edge both give the same value)

value(T) by Output enum:
  Lerp:   l0*v0 + l1*v1 + l2*v2, v_i = rnd11(hash of corner cell)  (C0 piecewise-linear 'jittered linear value noise')
  LerpSource: v_i = Source(P_i): mask-select the 3 corner positions first, then 3 source evaluations total
  Flat:   rnd11(hash(c, triIndex))  -> low-poly flat facets
  Plane:  h_T + Slope*dot(g_T, S - centroid_T), g_T random dir from table -> tilted facets (hillshade shows crystal planes)
  Tent:   3*min(l0,l1,l2) -> pyramid on every triangle, C0
  Packing: see CellularCirclePacking

3D: hexahedra H(c), c in {s-1,s}^3 (8 of them), Kuhn/Freudenthal 6-tet split along the main diagonal (consistent across shared faces because every hex uses the same global pattern). Per tet (q0..q3): 4 signed volumes via triple products give lambda and inside. 48 tet tests. Jitter clamped to <= 0.3 so no tet inverts (to verify in the prototype).
4D: 16 hypercubes x 24 simplices is too costly; propose 4D at jitter 0 located by coordinate sorting (like 4D simplex) so GenTileable2D still tiles, with a warning that 4D facets are lattice-regular.
master.why_new: CellularLookup evaluates its source per window cell and gives flat Voronoi tiles, so nothing yields C0 linear interpolation over irregular triangles. Evaluating the source only at the lane-specific n+1 vertices makes it much cheaper than a CellularLookup window.
master.simd_plan:
2D: 7 hashes, 6 barycentric solves sharing P_n, Select chain: about 2-3x Perlin. 3D: 15 vertices and 24 tetra around a vertex with Cramer solves: about 2x CellularDistance. 4D: the fan has 120 simplices, which is too costly, so use unjittered Kuhn simplex (sort coordinates like Simplex, 5 values) and accept regular creases in tiled output. Lookup adds n+1 source calls.
[CellularFacetMesh, cell-relations] Window loop as Cellular.inl for 9 / 27 points. Diagonal tests: 4 quads x ~25 ops (crosses + in-circle determinant). Triangles: 8 x (3 crosses, 3 compares, 1 rcp, Select accumulation) ~ 20 ops. Total ~300 ops: ~7 ns 2D (2x Cellular2D, 6x Perlin). 3D: 48 tets x ~60 ops ~ 3000 ops: ~80 ns (6-7x Cellular3D). An alternating 5-tet split (40 tets, all faces share the same diagonal choice via parity) trims ~20%. 4D as stated (regular Kuhn, ~2x 4D simplex cost).
master.continuity: C0 by construction (shared edges interpolate shared vertices). check: c0ratio 8.00 with max slope 4.35. The flat-id mode is discontinuous. Mode min/max also C0.
master.params: Jitter (constant; 2D <0.9, 3D <=0.3), Diagonal enum {Delaunay, Shorter, Random}, Output enum {Lerp, LerpSource, Flat, Plane, Tent, Packing}, Slope (hybrid, Plane mode), Source (GeneratorSource for LerpSource), Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
master.risks:
3D is expensive and the no-inversion jitter bound must be measured; 4D story is weak (regular lattice). Quad diagonals at low jitter show the grid. Thin triangles at high jitter give long sliver facets (Delaunay diagonal choice limits this).
[TriFacet, cell-relations] The 0.23 jitter bound keeps a faint triangular lattice bias, and the proto used a larger 0.28 with search, so the look at 0.23 needs confirming. Only the 2D form has been prototyped; 3D fan code is nontrivial. The 4D fallback has a different look when tiling. Hash ties with a square lattice plus in-circle diagonal choice are an alternative that gives more Delaunay-like triangles.
master.cost_note: 2D: 7 hashes, 6 barycentric solves sharing P_n, Select chain: about 2-3x Perlin. 3D: 15 vertices and 24 tetra around a vertex with Cramer solves: about 2x CellularDistance.
master.variant_notes: Two point locations: nearest vertex fan with bounded jitter 0.23 (TriFacet), or 2x2 quads with Delaunay diagonals (FacetMesh, up to 0.9). LerpSource gives low-poly of any node at n+1 evals.

queue.name: CellularFacetMesh
queue.reason: Pointwise jittered triangulation with Delaunay diagonals: low-poly without a regular lattice. 2D is fine and 3D tetra solves are heavy. Weigh against simplex-facet.

biome-blend.look: With textured biomes it looks good: soft natural borders, each biome's texture stays intact, no axis squareness. On a plain two level mask the truth shows: the border is scalloped at cell scale, a jittered staircase of bumps, because it follows point decisions rather than the control contour. At control wavelength 8 cells a straight diagonal border reads as serrated. Hard nearest point is ugly and jagged. Hash control gives cell sized blobs, not regions. Argmax control gives good regions with the same scallops. In 3D, plane mode gives columns with full 3D content inside, as designed, and a small biome becomes a tower. The full 27 point form gives terrain and cave mixtures that look fine.
biome-blend.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured in plane mode (9 evals) and full mode (27 evals). 4D not built and not viable: 81 evals at 3^4, and 2^4 only covers at jitter 0, which brings back squareness.
biome-blend.range: Convex combination of the sources, so the range is the union of source ranges. Measured -0.653..0.932 for the test biomes, -1..1 for constant levels. No NaN seen; total weight stays positive in the measured settings.
biome-blend.artifacts: Median width 0.86-0.90 cells over control wavelengths 4 to 64 (Fade 0.48 to 6.84), but local p95/p05 1.9-2.1, cv 0.19-0.22. Border offset from the control contour: median 0.18 cell, p95 0.46. 3x3 window shows no squareness (cos4t -0.027, isotropic reads -0.067); 2x2 is square (+0.626). Width is tied to Cell (R 1.07 gives 0.70, R 1.25 gives 0.96). Coverage: 2D proved at J .25, 0 holes in 400000 samples; 3D at J .25 has no proof (0 holes in 400000), J .2 R 1.25 proved. Sources per 8 lane batch 1.59-1.78 of 4 on coherent rows; incoherent lanes run all sources.
biome-blend.node_shape: BiomeBlend: Control, Sources 0..N (hybrid), Source Count, Cell Size, Radius (1.07..1.25), Jitter, Plane enum, no 4D. Only worth building for discontinuous or categorical controls; use DistFade for continuous controls and FoamBlend v2 for new regions.
biome-blend.port_notes: Window loop as Cellular.inl, Control once per point at its jittered position, N MaskedAdd per point, FS::AnyMask to skip a source for the batch. Control is about 90% of the node cost without sources. Offer a hash control path with no evals.

critic.notes: Transition width is not locally constant: the two-level border at seed 7 is visibly scalloped at cell scale and the wide view shows lumpy outlines, matching the prototyper's cv 0.2 and p95/p05 ~2 (not re-measured). Worse, the textured render shows a honeycomb cell mosaic wherever the control hovers near a biome threshold (the blend kernel of neighbouring points picking different biomes), which is a lattice imprint a technical artist would reject even though it is not square. 9 control evals for the control alone (17.5x perlin2) buys a worse border than DistFade (3 evals, 6x) and the plain Fade chain (2.5x). The one remaining case, categorical/discontinuous controls, is too narrow for a node. FoamBlend v2 at seed 7 has pointed cusps on its blobs and ringing in the FFT; it is a curiosity, not a replacement.

tournament.notes: Re-tested: check c0ratio 7.8, far coords ok; speed textured 1042 ns, control+weights 868 (claim 895), Fade chain 124, DistFade 296 (claim 316), FoamBlend v2 1061 (claim 1124): all confirmed. Two-level border at seed 7 is scalloped at cell scale with lumpy outlines in the wide view, so the width is constant only as a median (cv not re-measured). Textured render shows a honeycomb cell mosaic wherever the control is near a biome threshold: a lattice imprint not mentioned in the report. 9 control evals buy a worse border than DistFade (3 evals) or a plain Fade chain. DistFade is a graph of existing nodes and covers the continuous case; the categorical-control case is too narrow. FoamBlend v2 shows pointed cusps and FFT ringing at seed 7: a curiosity, not a node.

master.one_liner: Pointwise form of KdotJPG's scattered biome blending: N sources blended by normalised sparse convolution over jittered points, giving constant-width, non-square transitions.
master.look: Look-tested (mode 18, 4 sources): the hard version shows jagged cell biomes and the blended version gives smooth organic boundaries with each biome's own texture intact and no axis squareness.
master.algorithm: For cells c in the 3x3 window of floor(p/Cell): q = c + 0.5 + Jit*(rnd11, rnd11) with |Jit| <= 0.25. k = max(0, R^2 - |p/Cell - q|^2)^2 with R in [1.07, 1.25], so at least one point always contributes and none outside the window can. Then b = clamp(floor(Control(q*Cell)*N)), W[b] += k, tot += k. out = sum_b (W[b]/tot)*S_b(p). Same kernel max(0,r^2-d^2)^2 and dynamic normalisation as the source article, but per point rather than per chunk, with the window bound derived to fit FastNoise's lattice rule: p is at most (0.5+0.25)*sqrt2 = 1.06 from a point; points outside the window are at least 1.25 away.
master.why_new:
Common worldgen need. FastNoiseLite #91: three commenters say they had to write their own cell noise to place biomes per cell. The FastNoise2 wiki tells people to use CellularLookup/CellularValue for biome-like regions, which gives hard edges only. FastNoise2 #163 and discussion #162 are about blending many big trees. KdotJPG's write-up documents that grid interpolation shows squareness and full blur is slow, measuring 196 ns per coordinate for scattered at r=24 cells of 8. No graph can accumulate kernel weights by per-cell id: Fade is 2-way and CellularLookup returns only the nearest cell.
[BiomeScatter, libs-modifiers] Fade on a control node has transition width proportional to 1/|grad control|, so borders vary from razor sharp to continent-wide, and N biomes need a chain of N-1 Fades. KdotJPG's method assumes chunks and a linked list of weights; the pointwise window form obeys the handbook. Constant world-space blend width is a real authoring gain for worldgen.
master.simd_plan: Window*Control evals (9 in 2D) + cells*N MaskedAdd + active sources. A source is skipped when its W is zero for every lane (FS::AnyMask batch skip, output identical). 2D with 2-octave Perlin control: about 20 ns + active sources. 3D: use a plane mode (lattice in x,z, sources get full 3D), since biomes are columnar anyway, at the same 9 evals. Full 3D is 27 evals; 4D tiling needs a 2^4 window with R near 1 and small jitter, accepting weaker coverage, or is unsupported.
master.continuity:
C0: kernel reaches zero at R and is normalised by a strictly positive total. Measured c0ratio 8.0.
[BiomeBlend, repo-demand] C1 wherever total>0: w has zero slope at R and the quotient is smooth. Measured coverage holes (total=0) in the prototype at R=1 over a 256 cell window: about 0.05% of samples at jitter 1, about 0.01% or less at 0.8, none seen at 0.6. Default jitter 0.7, or add a small weight that follows the nearest cell, to remove the rare C0 break. Overall c0ratio 2.9 in the prototype but that includes the Worley and ridged test biomes.
master.params: Control (generator), Sources 0..7 (hybrid), Source Count (int), Cell Size, Radius R (clamped to safe range), Jitter (clamped), Plane enum, Contrast Preserve (bool).
master.risks:
Control runs 9x, so it needs to be cheap. Control detail below Cell size is lost, as with CellularLookup. R range is narrow, so blend width is tied to Cell. Fixed source slots make for a large node UI. Batch-skip gains shrink for incoherent lanes and when borders fill the batch.
[BiomeBlend, repo-demand] Member list is long and the editor needs variable pin count, since metadata has no variable sources. Borders wobble at the cell scale (author notes the same tradeoff). All N sources run for every batch that touches them. 4D tile cost is high. 3D coverage worst case is worse than 2D, so check jitter limits.
master.cost_note: 2D with 2-octave Perlin control: about 20 ns + active sources.
master.variant_notes: Two window bounds are in play: R up to 1 with Jitter 0.7 and rare holes (BiomeBlend measured 0.05% holes at jitter 1), or R in [1.07,1.25] with |Jitter|<=0.25 which guarantees coverage (BiomeScatter).
